newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest outshines other E.European bourses again.
newsitem.headline: Budapest outshines other E.European bourses again.

text.p: The Budapest bourse again took the spotlight among eastern European markets this week, making some of the strongest gains and setting a new all-time high.
Bratislava rose strongly after the approval of a new securities law to join the upwardly mobile Warsaw and Prague bourses. Prices dipped in Ljubljana and Bucharest, and were mixed in Zagreb.

Nervousness on Wall Street after last Friday's tumble left its impact on the region's markets. The Central European Share Index (CESI), which measures price movements of 73 Hungarian, Czech, Polish, Slovak and Slovenian stocks, advanced only 1.42 percent to 1,410.84 points.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian share prices rose every day, setting a new all-time high of 3,818.21 points on Friday to lock in a near three percent gain through the week.
The market moved mostly in line with other European markets, influenced by Wall Street, but also received support from the domestic macroeconomic side.
The chemicals firms and hotelier Danubius were high flyers with Danubius soaring to an all-time high of 3,945 forints on Thursday, after the Competition Office cleared its purchase of a hotel chain.

Oil and gas company MOL also performed well though its rising trend reversed on Thursday mainly amid uncertainties over the details of a wholesale energy price increase on January 1 -- but also after a sell rating by ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
WARSAW
The Polish bourse rose this week, but analysts expected it to drift sideways next week, despite anticipated speculative trading in some stocks ahead of company monthly earnings.
Analysts said the market could find resistance at about 14,000 points of the main index next week, still in its general month-long flat trend having fallen slightly last week.
The main market's WIG index closed at 13,706.3 points, up 1.3 percent from last Friday's close.
PRAGUE
Czech shares had a quiet week with activity falling sharply and the PX50 index ending the week close to where it began.
Dealers said foreign investors were standing on the sidelines while domestic buying had run out of steam, making for a slow pre-holiday market.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) saw a revival of foreign investor interest mainly as a result of the approval of a better-than-expected new securities law on Tuesday.
The 12-share SAX index reversed its three-month-long decline and rose 13.15 points to close at 181.09 on Friday.
"It looks as if foreign investors have regained confidence in the Slovak market after the passing of the law," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
The Slovak parliament on Tuesday amended securities legislation which investors feared could have had a disastrous effect on market transparency and its liquidity if passed in the original form.
But the new law omitted a clause which would have allowed major shareholders to arbitrarily cancel trading of an issue.
LJUBLJANA

In Ljubljana share prices dipped 0.6 percent but the market's biggest decliner, brokerage Dadas, sharply underperformed the market with a 27.6 percent plunge. The SBI index ended at 1,184.6 points, down 7.0.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks closed mostly lower on Friday on halved volume after mixed trading throughout the week, and analysts predicted dullness would plague the market till the year-end.

Some issues rebounded from losses of the past few weeks. Blue chip Pliva pharmaceuticals recovered to 13,000 kuna after dipping last week. Zagrebacka Banka held steady at 980-990 kuna but oscillated in line with its GDRs in London.
Traders said foreign investors could provide the impetus needed to pull the market out of its current depression but they appeared to hold back after the latest political stirrings.
BUCHAREST
Stronger buying in fertiliser maker Azomures SA pushed overall turnover on the Bucharest bourse higher to 96 million lei ($25,720) from last week's two-session level of 55 million.
But thin demand for other stocks drove most prices down, sending two independent indices to consecutive year lows.
The unofficial VAB and BIG indices fell from the previous session, slipping to year lows. The VAB dropped 2.9 percent to 273.4 points and the BIG was 2.86 percent down to 272.6 points.
TIRANA

The National Commercial Bank of Albania bought 50 million leks ($495,000) worth of 364-day treasury bills maturing at a yield of 17.5 percent from the Savings Bank on Monday, a Tirana Stock Exchange (TSE) official said.
Neither treasury bills nor state obligations changed hands on Thursday, the seven-month old TSE's second weekly session. "They could not agree on the yields," the official said.
